members.name: The Bull Weevils (briefly as lead singer)

podcast.title: Dilettante Pop Star Ambitions
podcast.body: Robert Wace, described as a "deletante wannabe pop star," initially sought The Bull Weevils as his backing band, arranging lucrative gigs at "society functions for his rich friends" in exchange for performing a couple of songs during their shows. However, his pop star aspirations proved unsuccessful, as he was "booed off stage" during a performance for an audience not composed of his friends, making it clear there was "no future" for him as a pop star. "It became clear that there was no future for Robert Ways as a pop star, but there was a future for the Bull Weevils."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 119: "You Really Got Me" by the Kinks

podcast.title: Funded "You Really Got Me" Re-recording
podcast.body: Robert Wace demonstrated faith in The Kinks' vision for "You Really Got Me" when Ray Davis vehemently disliked Shell Tauhmey's initial overproduced recording. He personally "paid for a new recording session out of his own pocket" after Larry Page insisted the original couldn't be released due to publishing rights, enabling the creation of the hit version. "Robert Wace paid for a new recording session out of his own pocket."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 119: "You Really Got Me" by the Kinks

podcast.title: Manager of The Kinks (Early)
podcast.body: After his own pop star career failed, Robert Wace, alongside his best friend Grenville Collins, agreed to manage The Bull Weevils (later The Kinks). Their management deal stipulated that Collins would invest half his stockbroker wages, and Wace and Collins would receive "50% of the group's earnings." "Ways and Collins would manage the group. Collins would put in half his wages from his job as a stockbroker, and Ways and Collins would get 50% of the group's earnings."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
